title: Standalone review squad
summary: A standalone review session MUST resolve one review target and capture it once. It MUST delegate a single review-squad coordinator over that capture. It MUST end with one ranked finding set and a verdict, and it MUST change no file.
instructions: The session MUST resolve exactly one review target before it captures anything. A target is a ref range or a pull request. A target can also be a ref range the operator narrowed to a named path set. The path set filters the capture. It never replaces the range the scope check runs on. When the request names no target, the session MUST derive the range from the current branch. The range runs against the merge base of that branch with the default branch. The session MUST state the range it chose. When the request is ambiguous rather than absent, the session MUST ask the operator instead of guessing.

The session MUST write the captured target to one file beside its governance card. The session MUST hand that path to the coordinator. A single capture keeps every dimension agent reading the same bytes. A target re-derived per agent lets the review drift.

Before delegating, the session MUST bind the review workspace to the target's head commit. The session MUST tell the coordinator which path that is. A dimension agent confirms a finding by reading the code around it. A workspace parked at another commit yields findings about files the capture never described. When the current checkout is not at that head, the session MUST resolve a worktree from that head. The session MUST NOT review against the wrong tree.

The session MUST run the harness review-scope check on the resolved target before it delegates. The session MUST act on each reported conflict by its tier. An instrument conflict is a change to the lineup, a charter, the coordinator, or the mode policy. An entry point, the scope check, and the reviewer's model mapping are also instrument conflicts. An instrument conflict leaves the squad's verdict. It goes to an independent reviewer that does not run the squad. The report MUST name it. A charter cannot find a defect introduced into that charter. A conduct conflict is a policy on the reviewer's own card or guidance it delivers. A conduct conflict stays in the squad's scope. The session MUST build its card with the base revision. Its conduct then follows the rule in force before the change. A substrate conflict is validation code, a test helper, or a check wrapper. The gate cache, an exemption registry, and the changelog are also substrate conflicts. A substrate conflict stays in scope. Every finding whose verification leans on such a file MUST say so.

A change to a standard MUST NOT be rejected for differing from the standard it replaces. When the target changes a policy, the report MUST carry a standards delta. The delta names each instruction the change removed and each instruction it added. The merits of that change belong to the operator as a decision distinct from the code that benefits from it. The squad judges whether the changed rule agrees with every surface it did not touch. The squad judges whether an agent can execute the changed rule. The squad does not judge whether the new rule is better.

The coordinator MUST derive the intent brief from the target's own artifacts. Those artifacts are commit subjects, the request, a linked card, or acceptance criteria. The session MUST supply those sources rather than the brief. Every finding dropped as already answered MUST quote the brief line that answers it. The quote lets the operator audit the drops.

When the conversation that runs the session authored any part of the target, the session MUST disclose that authorship. The report MUST carry the disclosure as a deviation. The session SHOULD hand the review to a fresh session. On a repeat review of the same target, dimension agents MUST review the delta blind. They MUST NOT see the prior finding set before they produce their findings. The coordinator reconciles afterwards.

The session MUST delegate exactly one review-squad coordinator per review round. That coordinator alone owns the lineup, the join, the ranking, and the verdict. A dimension agent the coordinator spawns is a nested spawn. A nested spawn runs on the platform default model, which is not acceptable for charter-scoped review work. The session MUST therefore issue the dimension fan-out itself, at the top level and in one message. The fan-out MUST use the charters, capture, workspace, and finding shape the coordinator resolved. The session MUST hand the raw findings back to the same coordinator. The session MUST name any charter whose subagent could not start. The coordinator MAY apply such a charter itself in join mode. The coordinator MUST record which charters it applied. The session MUST NOT join, rank, drop, or grade a finding itself. Each dimension prompt MUST carry the calibration bar and the boundaries from the squad procedure. Each dimension prompt MUST state that the agent edits no file, stages nothing, commits nothing, and pushes nothing. Each dimension prompt MUST state that the agent writes no workflow state.

The session MUST report which dimensions ran. The session MUST report which conditional dimensions the target did not activate. The session MUST report which charters the coordinator applied itself because a subagent could not start. A dimension that returned nothing MUST appear as empty rather than be omitted.

The session, the coordinator, each dimension agent, and the independent reviewer MUST NOT edit a file or stage a change. None of them MAY commit, push, or write workflow state. The independent reviewer is the agent the session delegates for the instrument tier. A standalone review yields findings only. Acting on a finding is a separate operator decision.

The session MUST close with one operator-facing report. The report MUST carry the resolved target and the ranked findings in the squad finding shape. The report MUST carry every dropped finding with its reason. The report MUST carry two verdicts. The coordinator verdict covers the graded tiers. The independent reviewer verdict covers the instrument tier. The report MUST state one combined outcome. The combined outcome is fail when either verdict is fail. When the target has no instrument conflict, the report MUST mark the instrument verdict as not applicable. A repeat of the independent verdict inside the report is not a graded finding.

guidance_sources.read_trigger: Read this guidance before you resolve the lineup, delegate a charter, or judge a finding.
